To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
five copies of Δ6- and Δ8- desaturase genes were identified and functionally analyzed, and the genes encoding Δ8-sphingolipid desaturation were identified for the first time in blackcurrant.
we identified and functionally characterized Δ6-desaturate from blackcurrant, which is a new member of this family of enzymes, and we identified the key amino acid residues that define its activity.

five nearly identical copies encoding Δ6-desaturation genes were identified from blackcurrant and that RnD8C/D/E are Δ6-desaturates, RnD 8A/B are Δ8-sphingolipid desatures, and Rn 6D is a Δ6-desaturate expressed in seeds and responsible for GLA and OTA synthesis in blackcurrant.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and functional characterization of Δ6-desatrase genes from blackcurrant, and the results provide the basis for further research on the molecular mechanism of GLA synthesis in blackcurrant.
the identification and functional analysis of blackcurrant Δ8- and Δ6-desaturates, the accumulation of GLAs in blackcurrant, and the evolutionary relationship among the desaturases.
the identification, cloning, and functional characterization of Δ6-desaturated genes in blackcurrant, which is an important oil plant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the blackcurrant RnD6 genes encode Δ6-desaturates, which are involved in the synthesis and accumulation of GLA.
RnD8 is a Δ8-sphingolipid desaturated, whereas RnDs are Δ6-desaturated, with RnD8 being the closest homologue to RnD6.
RnD8 and RnD8-like genes encode Δ8-sphingolipid desaturasases, whereas Rn6C, D and E encode Δ6-desaturates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have cloned the first Δ6-desaturate genes from a plant, blackcurrant, which can be used to produce GLA and OTA.
the Δ6-desaturation pathway is a complex system in blackcurrant and that the Δ6 pathway is a key pathway for GLA accumulation.
we have identified and characterized the first Δ6-desaturate genes from blackcurrant, which can be used for genetic improvement of blackcurrant and other plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RnD6 genes encode a Δ6-desaturate that is active in the ER of blackcurrant.
the blackcurrant RnD6 desaturases have a wide substrate specificity, and their expression patterns are consistent with their function in GLA biosynthesis.
blackcurrant seeds are an excellent source for GLA, and that the expression level of RnD6 genes in blackcurrant seeds is the key determinant of GLA accumulation in blackcurrant seed.
